docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
FIDO (Filtering and Identification of Dynamic Objects) is a dynamic-object rejection front-end built into GLIM, a versatile and extensible range-based 3D mapping framework. This repository is GLIM 1.3.0 with a fifth module tree, src/glim/dynamic_rejection/, added in place. The preprocessor gained a few options for FIDO (raw scan kept for the rejection, uniform sampling, neighbours always computed); odometry/, mapping/ and viewer/ are upstream GLIM.

FIDO intercepts raw LiDAR scans before they reach GLIM's odometry front-end, splits each point cloud into a static subset forwarded to GLIM and a dynamic subset held back for diagnostics, and keeps pedestrians, vehicles and other moving agents out of the scan-matching factors and the reconstructed map.

  • Two independent filters: a voxel-based, detector-free pipeline (Module 1) and a supervised bounding-box pipeline (Module 2) — selectable, or combinable, per session via dynamic_rejection_type.
  • Evidence, not thresholds on one frame: per-voxel centroid shift against a noise model, free space in past range images and in a world free-space map, and vacated space behind a moving track; aggregated per object by a tracker with evidence accumulation and releasable locks.
  • Works with or without IMU: the pose of each scan is predicted at constant velocity when no IMU is available.
  • Decoupled from SLAM: FIDO runs as a producer–consumer background thread (AsyncDynamicObjectRejection), so filtering never blocks scan acquisition, and CPU-only, so GLIM's GPU stays dedicated to scan matching.
  • Everything else is stock GLIM: direct multi-scan registration error minimization on factor graphs, GPU-accelerated scan matching, interactive map correction, and support for any range sensor (spinning LiDAR, non-repetitive scan LiDAR, solid-state LiDAR, RGB-D).

Tip

New here? Start with Quickstart for the build-and-run path, or jump straight to Architecture to see how FIDO's background thread fits into GLIM's pipeline. Tuning guide and Evaluation cover adapting FIDO to a new sensor and measuring it.

docs.title: The two modules
docs.text: Module Mode What it does Module 1 — Voxel-based Autonomous Geometry-only pipeline: uniform rejection frame → ground/wall filtering → DBSCAN clustering + tracking → voxel evidence (shift, free space, vacated space) → object decision → point labels transferred to the odometry frame. Needs no external detector. Module 2 — Bounding-box Supervised Consumes oriented 3D boxes from an external detector/tracker over a ROS 2 topic and strips every point inside a velocity-inflated footprint.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: FIDO runs as a producer–consumer system decoupled from GLIM's preprocessing thread, so scan filtering never blocks scan acquisition. The producer pushes a frame with insert_frame(), which wakes a background thread (a condition variable, no polling); the thread drains every queued frame in order, runs the voxel pipeline and hands the results back through mutex-protected queues — static frames, dynamic frames, wall results, cluster boxes — or, if one is set, through an output callback for the static frame.

docs.title: Clustering runs before scoring
docs.text:
Per frame, in order:

  1. set_frame_stamp() — selects the pose of this scan (Ego-motion).
  2. make_rejection_frame() — uniform sample of the raw scan plus far extra points.
  3. WallFilter::filter() — voxel map with ground, wall and outlier flags.
  4. DynamicClusterExtractor::extract_clusters() — clusters and tracks, plus get_dynamic_track_history() (past boxes of confirmed tracks).
  5. DynamicObjectRejectionCPU::reject() — voxel evidence, object decision, point labels.
  6. transfer_labels() — labels copied onto the odometry frame.
  7. update_dynamic_feedback() — the per-frame verdicts go back to the tracker.

Clustering runs before scoring because reject() takes the boxes as input:

DynamicObjectRejectionCPU::reject(wf, frame, cluster_bboxes, historical_bboxes)

so per-voxel scoring already knows which voxels sit inside corroborated dynamic evidence — this is what lets Module 1's tiered threshold work. After scoring, update_dynamic_feedback(cluster_bboxes) writes the outcome back into each track's counters and evidence, closing the loop for the next frame.

Header comment vs. actual order

async_dynamic_object_rejection.hpp's doc comment still lists the steps as WallFilter → reject → extract_clusters. The runtime order is the one above.

docs.title: Ego-motion
docs.text:
Every stage reads the absolute pose of the current scan from PoseKalmanFilter::getFramePose(): it compensates ego-motion against the stored history, moves past boxes and wall boxes into the current sensor frame, and drives the free-space map.

  • With IMU — an error-state Kalman filter (9-dim: δp, δv, δθ) integrates the IMU between SLAM pose updates and fuses each new SLAM pose.
  • Without IMU — the filter keeps the last two stamped SLAM poses (update(T, stamp)) and extrapolates them at constant velocity to the scan stamp set by set_frame_stamp(), up to 1 s. On HeLiMOS this matches the dataset poses (IoU < 20 m 72.8 against 73.3); using the last pose without prediction drops it to 62.4.

The filter has no config keys: noise matrices and the extrapolation limit are fixed in transformation_kalman_filter.cpp.

docs.title: Scope of this repository
docs.text: This repository builds libglim.so and its plugin modules (odometry, mapping, viewer, dynamic rejection) — the algorithms and the JSON schema they read. The ROS 2 node that instantiates AsyncDynamicObjectRejection / DynamicBBoxRejection, subscribes to sensor topics, and publishes the diagnostic point clouds lives in FIDO-GLIM-ROS2 — a companion workspace package, also maintained as part of this project, that links against this library. It's cloned and built alongside this repo, not merged into it — see Installation — and no publisher/subscriber code exists inside this repository itself.

docs.title: Docker images
docs.text:
docker/ubuntu/ ships two equivalent Dockerfiles — Dockerfile.gcc and Dockerfile.llvm — on top of nvidia/cuda:13.1.0-devel-ubuntu24.04, targeting ROS 2 Jazzy. Each one:

  1. Installs the ROS base + build tooling (libfmt-dev, libspdlog-dev, libopencv-dev, Boost, Eigen3, GLFW/GLM/PNG/JPEG for the viewer).
  2. Adds the koide3/iridescence and koide3/gtsam PPAs, and installs libiridescence-dev / libgtsam-no-tbb-dev.
  3. Clones and installs gtsam_points from source with -DBUILD_WITH_CUDA=${WITH_CUDA}.
  4. Copies this repository in and builds it twice — once headless (BUILD_WITH_VIEWER=OFF) and once with the viewer on — so both image variants are validated in one pass.
docker build -f docker/ubuntu/Dockerfile.gcc \
  --build-arg WITH_CUDA=ON \
  --build-arg ROS_DISTRO=jazzy \
  -t fido-glim:gcc .
Build arg Default Purpose BASE_IMAGE nvidia/cuda:13.1.0-devel-ubuntu24.04 Base image (swap for a plain ubuntu:24.04 for a CPU-only image). WITH_CUDA OFF Passed straight through to gtsam_points's and FIDO-GLIM's own -DBUILD_WITH_CUDA. ROS_DISTRO jazzy ROS 2 distribution installed inside the image.

Note

Dockerfile.gcc and Dockerfile.llvm differ only in the compiler toolchain installed — both otherwise follow the same steps and produce equivalent images.

docs.title: Offline harness — kitti_dynamic_eval
docs.text:
Runs exactly the steps of AsyncDynamicObjectRejection::run() on a sequence in SemanticKITTI layout, without ROS, and writes the per-point labels on the original scan indices, so they can be compared with the .label files directly.

Build:

cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_TESTS=ON
make -j kitti_dynamic_eval

Run:

kitti_dynamic_eval --config <glim config dir> --seq <sequences/NN> --poses <poses/NN.txt> \
                   --out <dir> --pose_mode ros_cv [--start 0 --end N]
Option Meaning --pose_mode exact pose of the current frame from the dataset (upper bound) --pose_mode lag --lag N pose of frame i−N --pose_mode ros glim_ros without IMU, old behaviour: unstamped update with the pose of frame i−1 --pose_mode ros_cv / ros_cv2 current glim_ros without IMU: stamped update with the pose of frame i−1 / i−2, constant-velocity prediction to the scan stamp --raw_max N random subset of the raw scan --uniform_frame N bypass the GLIM preprocessor: the frame is N uniform raw points beyond 1 m --diag 1 also rej/NNNNNN.diag (per-point flags) and rej/NNNNNN.boxes (decision inputs of every box) --dump_input DIR write the rejection input of every frame, to run other methods on the same points

Every flag takes a value. Poses are converted to the Velodyne frame with T = Tr⁻¹ · P · Tr (calib.txt), stamps come from times.txt.

Outputs: <out>/NNNNNN.pred (int32 n, then n × {int32 original index, uint8 dynamic}) for the odometry frame, <out>/rej/NNNNNN.pred for the rejection's own points, per-stage timings on stdout.

Use a config with dynamic_rejection_type set

The preprocessor keeps the raw scan only when dynamic_rejection_type in config_ros.json is not "NONE". With the shipped config_ros.json ("NONE") the harness silently runs without the uniform rejection frame, the far extra points and the raw range images, and writes nothing to rej/. Point --config to a copy with "dynamic_rejection_type": "CLUSTER".

docs.title: Metrics — kitti_dynamic_eval.py
docs.text:
python3 test/kitti_dynamic_eval.py --seq <sequences/NN> --pred <out> [--json res.json] \
        [--radius 0.5] [--ignore 0 1] [--frames split.txt]
  • Moving = label ids 251–259 (lower 16 bits).
  • Sampled: metrics on the classified points. Full scan: every scan point takes the label of the nearest classified point within --radius, otherwise static.
  • P / R / IoU / F1 per range band (0–10, 10–20, 20–50, 0–20, 0–50 m, all), per-frame mean IoU, mean dynamic share, frames above 10% dynamic, and the most frequent false-positive classes.

test/run_kitti_offline.sh <seq> <tag> [config,…] [modes…] stages a sequence, runs every config × pose mode in the container, evaluates and saves results, configs and commit hash. Its paths (NAS, container name) are those of the lab machine and must be adapted.

docs.title: Common pitfalls
docs.text:
These explain results that look like random labels (precision of a few percent):

  1. Labels compared by index on GLIM's output. GLIM drops and reorders points; the static and dynamic frames are separate lists. Always evaluate on the original points (the harness does), and check that frames are not shifted.
  2. Pose not predicted. Without IMU and without stamped updates, the rejection of scan t uses the pose of t−1: at 10 m/s that is ~1 m of ego-motion error and whole façades appear to move. Use ros_cv.
  3. Wrong extrinsic or pose convention. apply_lidar_imu_extrinsic: true applies your robot's T_lidar_imu; on a public dataset set it to false. KITTI poses are in the left-camera frame and must be converted with Tr.
  4. Semantic instead of moving labels. Parked cars are static in SemanticKITTI MOS; use the moving classes.
  5. Per-point times. KITTI .bin scans have no per-point time and are already motion-compensated; do not deskew them with made-up times.

Quick diagnosis: dynamic share per frame low (1–3%) but precision ~7% → evaluation problem (1); high (10–40%) → pose, extrinsic or deskew (2, 3, 5).

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Runs of 1–20 Oct 2026, labels on every point of the scan: HeLiMOS official test split (514 frames), label 0 ignored, pooled IoU; DOALS per-frame mean over the 10 annotated frames of each sequence (%); SemanticKITTI label 0 ignored, pooled. FIDO runs in this harness with dataset poses and ros_cv-style constant-velocity prediction, one configuration for every dataset except the clustering distance (eps_range_k 0.04 VLP-16, 0.010 OS1-64, 0.008 HDL-64, 0.0035 OS2-128; on the VLP-16 also visibility_min_filter_rows: 4).

docs.title: Moving-object IoU
docs.text:
Dataset IoU all ranges IoU within 20 m Precision Recall HeLiMOS KAIST05, Ouster OS2-128 0.53 0.61 0.84 0.60 HeLiMOS KAIST05, Velodyne VLP-16 0.35 0.37 0.89 0.36 DOALS (8 sequences, %) 73.9 77.4 — — SemanticKITTI 08 0.26 0.28 0.29 0.72

DOALS per scene, per-frame mean IoU (%), all ranges / within 20 m: Station 69.9 / 77.4, Shopville 71.4 / 72.7, HG 77.6 / 79.7, Niederdorf 76.7 / 79.7.

CrossLab — our robot (VLP-16 at 1.07 m, IMU) in a motion-capture room, 11 sequences, 6 300 scans, one person walking 0.7–6 m from the sensor; labels generated from Qualisys (points within 0.45 m of the person's vertical axis), pooled: precision 0.95, recall 0.95, IoU 0.900.

Before the lock release on static structure (locked_struct_frac, struct_min_age, permanent_release_no_motion_frames) FIDO reached 0.753 here: a track locked dynamic on the person was handed over to a cabinet and kept removing furniture for over 100 frames. On the other datasets the release changes IoU by −0.001 to +0.005.

docs.title: Effect on GLIM's trajectory
docs.text:
RMSE against the reference poses, ATE after SE(3) alignment, RPE over 1 m.

  • DOALS (8 sequences): unchanged within ±2% except Shopville, the scene with the most pedestrians close to the sensor, where RPE drops by 13–17% and ATE by up to 10%.
  • HeLiMOS Ouster (whole KAIST05, 6.9 km): ATE 2.23 vs 2.20 m, same local drift; FIDO keeps up with real time over all 12 466 scans.
  • HeLiMOS VLP-16: LiDAR-only odometry at car speed drifts ~9 m per 100 m either way and the median step error is the same, but with the range-dependent clustering distance FIDO doubles the rare large jumps (RPE RMSE 25 instead of 14 cm/m).
  • CrossLab (against Qualisys): mean ATE 2.5 vs 2.4 cm, RPE 3.6 cm/m in both.
  • Marina di Pisa (robot standing still on a street, 18 min, GPU odometry with IMU): largest excursion 5.0 vs 7.4 mm, end-to-start offset 2.6 vs 5.6 mm, per-scan jitter −10%; ATE around the mean 1.45 vs 1.37 mm.

docs.title: Which dynamic_rejection_type should I use?
docs.text: BBOX if you already run a reliable 3D object detector/tracker and want the cheapest possible filter. CLUSTER (Module 1) if you have no detector, or want geometry-only coverage. COMBINED when both are available — Module 2's boxes suppress the clear cases fast, Module 1 still scores what's left.

docs.title: What does env_type actually change?
docs.text: Currently nothing. It selects which peer_merge_distance_* value DynamicClusterExtractor loads, but the peer merge is bypassed by the fragment merge (frag_merge_gap ≥ 0), which fuses fragments by gap and object size regardless of the environment.

docs.title: Is FIDO GPU-accelerated?
docs.text: No — every stage in dynamic_rejection/ is CPU-bound (OpenMP or TBB, chosen by gtsam_points::is_omp_default() at runtime, matching whichever threading backend gtsam_points itself was built with). GPU cycles stay dedicated to GLIM's scan-matching factors.

docs.title: How does this relate to upstream GLIM?
docs.text: This repository is GLIM 1.3.0 with src/glim/dynamic_rejection/ added as a fifth module tree and five new JSON configs. The preprocessor has a few FIDO options (raw scan kept for the rejection, uniform sampling, raw_points_target, neighbours always computed); odometry/, mapping/ and viewer/ are upstream. It's meant to be built in place of koide3/glim, not alongside it.

docs.title: What hardware was FIDO tested on?
docs.text:
An AgileX Bunker Pro tracked UGV:

  • LiDAR — Velodyne VLP-16, 16 beams, ±15° vertical FoV, 10 Hz, ±3 cm accuracy
  • IMU — 6-DoF, rigidly co-mounted with the LiDAR
  • Stack — ROS 2 Jazzy, Ubuntu 24.04

On indoor and outdoor sequences under both static and moving-robot conditions, FIDO reduces pose drift and map ghost artifacts against an unfiltered GLIM baseline — Module 1 and Module 2 combined (COMBINED) outperform either alone by exploiting their complementary strengths: fast detector-driven removal plus geometry-driven coverage of what the detector misses.

docs.title: Can I run FIDO without an IMU?
docs.text: Yes. Use the CT odometry (config_odometry_ct.json) and make sure the pose updates reaching PoseKalmanFilter are stamped: the pose of each scan is then predicted at constant velocity. Without prediction the rejection uses a pose one scan old, and static structure appears to move. See Module 1, step 0.

docs.title: How do I measure FIDO on a dataset?
docs.text: With the offline harness kitti_dynamic_eval (build flag BUILD_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_TESTS), which evaluates on the original scan points. See Evaluation, including the pitfalls that make results look like random labels.

docs.title: Why does a 16-beam LiDAR give much lower recall?
docs.text: The evidence is geometric: with 2° between rings a pedestrian far away is a few points on one or two rings, the range images have empty rows, and clusters break up. Use visibility_min_filter_rows, eps_range_k and the other settings in Tuning guide; beyond ~20 m a VLP-16 currently yields almost no detections.

docs.title: Where's the ROS 2 node that publishes FIDO's diagnostic clouds?
docs.text: Not in this repository — it's in FIDO-GLIM-ROS2, a companion repository cloned and built alongside this one. See Installation and Architecture.

docs.title: Cite
docs.text:

docs.text:
Tip

Prebuilt Docker images are available if you'd rather skip building from source.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Dependency Notes ROS 2 Jazzy+ Communication layer for the FIDO-GLIM-ROS2 node Eigen3, Boost (serialization) Linear algebra, map serialization GTSAM ≥ 4.2 Factor graph backend gtsam_points ≥ 1.2.0 Factor graph extensions, KdTree, point-cloud & voxelmap types OpenMP or TBB Parallel per-voxel scoring — whichever backend gtsam_points was built with spdlog Structured logging (every FIDO stage logs through it) Iridescence (optional) Only required if BUILD_WITH_VIEWER=ON OpenCV (optional) Only required if BUILD_WITH_OPENCV=ON (camera-image support)

docs.title: Ubuntu PPAs
docs.text:
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:koide3/iridescence
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:koide3/gtsam
sudo apt update
sudo apt install libiridescence-dev libgtsam-no-tbb-dev

docs.title: gtsam_points
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/koide3/gtsam_points
cd gtsam_points && mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_WITH_CUDA=ON   # OFF for a CPU-only build
make -j$(nproc)
sudo make install

docs.title: Build FIDO-GLIM
docs.text:
FIDO-GLIM replaces upstream koide3/glim in your ROS 2 workspace — clone it as glim, not alongside it.

cd ~/ros2_ws/src
git clone https://github.com/giacomotambe/FIDO-GLIM.git glim

cd ~/ros2_ws
colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select glim

source install/setup.bash

Package name

package.xml declares the package as glim (version 1.3.0), so --packages-select glim is what colcon actually resolves.

docs.title: Build the ROS 2 node — FIDO-GLIM-ROS2
docs.text:
This repository only builds libglim.so and its plugin modules — it has no glim_rosnode/glim_rosbag executables and no publishers/subscribers of its own (see Architecture). Those live in a separate, companion repository, FIDO-GLIM-ROS2, which must be cloned into the same workspace and built against the glim package above.

cd ~/ros2_ws/src
git clone https://github.com/giacomotambe/FIDO-GLIM-ROS2.git

cd ~/ros2_ws
colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select glim glim_ros

source install/setup.bash

Once both are built and sourced, ros2 run glim_ros glim_rosnode / glim_rosbag are available — see Getting started.

Two repositories, one workspace

FIDO-GLIM (this repo) is the SLAM + dynamic-rejection library. FIDO-GLIM-ROS2 is the ROS 2 wrapper around it — the node, its launch files, and the topic publishers/subscribers. Both need to sit side by side under ~/ros2_ws/src for colcon build to resolve the dependency between them.

docs.title: Standalone CMake build
docs.text:
mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
         -DBUILD_WITH_CUDA=ON \
         -DBUILD_WITH_VIEWER=ON \
         -DBUILD_WITH_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_BBOX=ON
make -j$(nproc)
sudo make install

docs.title: Build options
docs.text:
Option Default Effect BUILD_WITH_CUDA ON Compiles odometry_estimation_gpu.cpp; falls back to OFF with a warning if gtsam_points wasn't built with CUDA. BUILD_WITH_CUDA_MULTIARCH OFF Cross-architecture GPU build. BUILD_WITH_VIEWER ON Builds standard_viewer, interactive_viewer, map_editor, memory_monitor against Iridescence. BUILD_WITH_OPENCV ON Camera-image support; defines GLIM_USE_OPENCV. BUILD_WITH_MARCH_NATIVE OFF Adds -march=native to C/C++ flags. BUILD_WITH_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_BBOX ON Compiles Module 2 in; sets GLIM_USE_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_BBOX=1. BUILD_WITH_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_VOXEL OFF Compiles Module 1's standalone define in; sets GLIM_USE_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_VOXEL=1. Mutually exclusive with the BBOX flag — BBOX wins if both are ON. BUILD_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_TESTS OFF Builds test_dynamic_rejection and the offline harness kitti_dynamic_eval — see Evaluation.

Reading the CMake carefully

All dynamic_rejection/*.cpp sources are compiled unconditionally into libglim regardless of these two flags — they only toggle the GLIM_USE_DYNAMIC_REJECTION_* preprocessor defines consumers can branch on. A separate BUILD_WITH_DYNAMIC_REJECTION guard also appears further down in CMakeLists.txt guarding GLIM_USE_DYNAMIC_REJECTION, but no matching option() ever sets it — that branch is effectively dead. The two flags above are the ones that do something.

Which module actually runs is a separate, runtime decision — see dynamic_rejection_type in Configuration files.

docs.title: Module 1 — Voxel pipeline
docs.text:
Autonomous — needs no external detector.

Module 1 splits every scan into a static frame (sent to GLIM odometry) and a dynamic frame (held back). The decision is built in three layers:

  1. per voxel — local evidence of motion (centroid shift, free space, vacated space);
  2. per object — voxels are grouped into clusters, clusters are tracked over time and confirmed dynamic only when the evidence holds;
  3. per point — the object decision is written back to the points, and from the rejection's own sample onto the odometry frame.
flowchart LR
  S[scan] --> P[pose of the scan<br/>PoseKalmanFilter]
  S --> R[rejection frame<br/>10k raw points + far extras]
  R --> W[WallFilter<br/>ground, walls, outliers]
  W --> C[clusters + tracks]
  C --> E[voxel evidence<br/>shift · range images · free-space map]
  E --> D[object decision<br/>+ vacated space]
  D --> L[point labels]
  L --> T[label transfer<br/>to the odometry frame]
  T --> O[static → GLIM<br/>dynamic → diagnostics]
  D --> F[tracker feedback]
  F -.-> C

Everything below runs inside AsyncDynamicObjectRejection::run(), in this order. Defaults are the values shipped in config/.

docs.title: 0 · Pose of the scan — PoseKalmanFilter
docs.text:
Every stage reads the pose of the current scan from PoseKalmanFilter::getFramePose() (times T_imu_lidar when apply_lidar_imu_extrinsic is true).

  • With IMU — the filter integrates the IMU between SLAM updates; the pose is the IMU-propagated one.
  • Without IMU — the filter keeps the last two stamped SLAM poses and extrapolates them at constant velocity to the scan stamp (set_frame_stamp), up to 1 s.

The pose of the current scan must be predicted

The rejection of scan t runs before odometry has processed t. If the pose is simply the last odometry pose (one scan behind, no prediction), static structure appears to move: on HeLiMOS IoU < 20 m drops from 72.8 to 62.4. Use an IMU, or stamped updates so the constant-velocity prediction kicks in.

docs.title: 1 · Rejection frame — make_rejection_frame
docs.text:
The rejection does not work on the odometry frame (which GLIM downsamples with a random grid). It builds its own input from the raw scan kept by the preprocessor:

Step Keys Default Uniform random sample of the raw scan (1–100 m), seeded by the stamp rej_input_points 10000 Extra raw points far away, used only to decide (marked with time = NaN) hybrid_enabled, hybrid_min_range, hybrid_max_range, hybrid_max_points on, 20–40 m, 8000 Past range images built from the raw scan vis_raw, vis_raw_max_range, vis_raw_max_points on, 70 m, 60000

A uniform sample keeps the sensor's density profile, which the evidence below depends on. At the end the labels are transferred back to the odometry frame (step 8), so GLIM still receives exactly its own points.

Note

The preprocessor attaches the raw scan only when dynamic_rejection_type in config_ros.json is not "NONE" and one of hybrid_enabled, vis_raw, fs_raw is on. Without it, the three steps above silently fall back to the odometry frame.

docs.title: 2 · Static structure — WallFilter
docs.text:
WallFilter::filter() voxelizes the rejection frame once (voxel_resolution, 0.25 m, Gaussian statistics per voxel) and flags structure, which is never dynamic:

  1. Ground, every frame. Polar grid over voxel centroids (10° sectors × 0.5 m bins); per sector a seed cell between 2 and 15 m, propagated inwards and outwards while the slope stays below floor_polar_slope_threshold and the height below floor_polar_max_ground_height. A RANSAC plane is then fitted to the ground voxels; its box defines is_ground.
  2. Walls. Vertical 2-point RANSAC on the non-ground voxels (wall_vertical_ransac), up to max_planes planes. Wall planes are turned into oriented boxes and merged into the WallBBoxRegistry, which persists across frames (matched by normal, centre distance and OBB IoU; union of the boxes, thickness clamped to max_wall_thickness). Voxels inside a registry box get is_wall.
  3. Outliers. Voxels behind a registry wall, seen from the sensor, get is_outlier.

Height above ground (HAG) for the later stages is computed separately: the lowest voxel centroid in the 3×3 block of ground_cell_m (2 m) cells around each voxel.

docs.title: 3 · Clusters and tracks — DynamicClusterExtractor
docs.text:
1. DBSCAN on voxels — non-structural voxels within cluster_max_range (70 m) and below cluster_max_height (4 m) above ground; neighbours found with a voxel hash; eps = eps_voxel_factor × voxel_resolution (0.375 m). eps_range_k optionally widens eps along z far from the sensor, for sparse rings (VLP-16 ≈ 0.04).
  2. Boxes — one AABB per cluster, filtered by size (bbox_min_extent 0.1 m – bbox_max_extent 4 m) and volume.
  3. NMS, then fragment merge — two boxes merge if their gap is < frag_merge_gap + frag_merge_gap_k · r (0.5 m + 0.02·r) and the union stays object-sized (frag_max_len/wid/hgt 6 × 3 × 4 m). The merged box remembers its parts, so points are later labelled only inside the parts.
  4. Tracking — tracks are predicted at constant velocity; boxes are associated by Hungarian assignment on centroid distance, with gate assoc_gate_base + assoc_gate_per_range · r + assoc_gate_per_missed · missed (0.8 + 0.03·r + 0.3·missed), solved per connected component. Unmatched tracks coast for up to track_max_missed (5) frames.

A track is confirmed dynamic when any of these holds:

Rule Keys Default Consecutive dynamic frames (hysteresis) min_dynamic_frames 2 Leaky evidence accumulator: e ← decay·e + (evidence − bias), confirmed when e ≥ on track_evidence_decay, _bias, _on, _max 0.8, 0.6, 0.5, 2.0 Locked state after N dynamic frames permanent_dynamic_frames 8

The accumulator confirms small or far objects that never pass the single-frame test, while the bias keeps the noise of static clusters out.

Locks and their release. After permanent_dynamic_frames (8) dynamic frames a track is locked dynamic; after permanent_static_frames (20) static frames it is locked static. Locks are not final:

  • a static lock is released after permanent_unlock_frames (2) frames of strong motion (dynamic ratio > unlock_ratio_factor × threshold, or vacated space);
  • a dynamic lock is released after permanent_release_no_motion_frames (3) matched frames without own motion — e.g. when the track has been handed over to a cabinet or a wall;
  • a locked-dynamic cluster is not removed in a frame if it lies for ≥ locked_struct_frac (70%) on static structure of the free-space map (cells occupied for struct_min_age frames and never seen free since), or if its box is taller than locked_max_height (2.5 m).

docs.title: 4 · Voxel evidence — DynamicObjectRejectionCPU
docs.text:
The module keeps 14 frames of history (voxel maps, poses, range images). For every non-structural voxel above the ground band (ground_band_m, 0.25 m):

a. Centroid shift against t−5 (compare_baseline_frames). The past voxel is found after ego-motion compensation, and the shift beyond a noise dead zone is scored:

σ(r)  = min(noise_sigma_max, noise_sigma0 + noise_sigma_slope · r)
        + pose_err_trans_k · ‖t_baseline‖ + pose_err_rot_k · θ_baseline · r
score = w_shift · max(0, |shift| − noise_deadzone_k · σ(r)) / voxel_resolution

Defaults: σ0 0.045 m, slope 0.007, max 0.10 m, k = 3, w_shift 1.2. The σ model is sensor-specific and is the first thing to re-tune on a new LiDAR.

b. Free space in past range images. Each point is projected into the range images of the scans at t−6, t−10, t−14 (visibility_min_age, _max_age, _age_step; 0.5° cells, 3×3 minimum filter). If the sensor used to see farther along that ray (by more than max(visibility_abs_thr, visibility_rel_thr · d) = max(0.3 m, 3%)), the point now occupies space that was free. A strict majority of the scans that see the cell decides. The voxel's vis is the fraction of its points that appeared in free space.

c. Free-space world map (fs_enabled). A sharded hash grid in the world frame (fs_res 0.3 m) counts, frame after frame, how often each cell was crossed by a ray (free) or hit (occupied). A point is evidence of motion if its cell was seen free ≥ fs_min_free (5) times and ≥ fs_free_ratio (5) × occupied, and all 26 neighbours are free too (fs_dilate, a DUFOMap-like dilation — without it poles and edges are "emptied" by rays). It gives long memory without storing scans. vis becomes the maximum of (b) and (c). Rays are integrated in parallel, one every fs_ray_stride (4) points, up to fs_max_range (60 m).

Score and thresholds. score += w_visibility · vis (0.5); score −= w_history · (fraction of the last frames where the voxel was static) (0.3). The voxel is dynamic if the score passes a three-tier threshold on dynamic_score_threshold (0.08):

Condition Factor Threshold Inside a dynamic box (or its velocity-inflated zone) tier1_threshold_factor 0.55 0.044 Dynamic at t−1 memory_threshold_factor 0.70 0.056 Isolated unconstrained_threshold_factor 3.0 0.24

A voxel with no match in the past is decided by free space alone. Dynamic voxels then add w_neighbor (0.2) to their 26 neighbours.

docs.title: 5 · Object decision — propagate_to_clusters
docs.text:
For each box: ratio = dynamic voxels / voxels, vis = mean free-space fraction. The cluster is dynamic in this frame if

  • ratio > cluster_propagation_threshold (0.45), and
  • shape is plausible: height ≥ min_obj_height (0.2 m), lowest point ≤ max_obj_bottom_hag (1.5 m) and highest ≤ max_obj_top_hag (2.3 m) above ground, and
  • it moves: track speed ≥ min_obj_speed (0.1 m/s) or vis ≥ moving_vis_alt (0.3), and
  • it was seen in free space: vis ≥ min_obj_vis (0.3);

or it passes the vacated-space test (vac_enable): the points the track occupied ≥ vac_gap_frames (8) frames ago, after a displacement ≥ vac_min_disp (0.6 m), are now seen through by the current scan (≥ 80% of the visible ones, ≥ 4 points), with a constant-velocity check on the midpoint. This catches objects whose own points carry little evidence.

This per-frame verdict is fed back to the tracker (step 3). A box is removed in the current frame only if its track is already confirmed, or by fast confirmation (ratio > 2 × threshold and vis ≥ 0.2).

Optional, off by default: delayed decision (fut_delay > 0) — wait D frames and also test the points against the future range images. On HeLiMOS fut_delay: 10 raised IoU < 20 m by about 2 points, at the cost of 1 s of latency (offline mapping only).

docs.title: 6 · Point labels
docs.text:
• Voxels inside the parts of a removed box → dynamic. A foot rule keeps near-ground voxels (HAG ≥ foot_min_hag, 0.10 m) under a tall confirmed box dynamic.
  • Voxels in the velocity-inflated zone of a dynamic box (config_bbox_rejection.json) or in recent boxes of confirmed tracks → dynamic only with their own evidence (inflated_requires_evidence).
  • Beyond point_ground_cut_min_range (10 m), points less than point_ground_cut (0.2 m) above ground stay static: they are ground returns inside the box.
  • Everything else is static: at default the output is decided per object, never by isolated voxels.
  • Anomalous-frame guard: if more than frame_max_dynamic_frac (10%) of the points come out dynamic — typically a pose error — only the bases of confirmed objects are kept dynamic.

docs.title: 7 · Memory update
docs.text: The voxel map, pose and range image of the frame enter the history (14 frames); the scan is integrated into the free-space map (after the query, so a scan never votes on itself).

docs.title: 8 · Label transfer — transfer_labels
docs.text: The labels found on the rejection frame are copied onto the odometry frame: each odometry point takes the label of its nearest labelled point within label_transfer_radius (0.5 m), static on ties and when nothing is within reach. The static frame reuses the preprocessing neighbours wherever possible, so GLIM's covariance estimation is not repeated.

docs.title: What changed from the first version
docs.text: The first version scored each voxel against the previous frame only (w_shift, w_cluster, w_distance, ego-motion-scaled thresholds) and propagated a cluster as soon as its dynamic ratio crossed a threshold. The current pipeline adds the noise dead zone, free space (range images and world map), vacated space, Hungarian tracking with evidence accumulation and lock release, the separate uniform rejection frame and label transfer, and the pose prediction without IMU. The legacy keys are still read but set to 0 — see Configuration reference.

docs.title: Module 2 — Bounding-box pipeline
docs.text:
Supervised — consumes an external detector/tracker's boxes.

DynamicBBoxRejection is deliberately simple: it holds a list of externally-supplied BoundingBoxes, ages them, and removes any point that falls inside one.

reject() ages every stored box each call (bbox_ages_[i] < max_bbox_frames_), then tests every point against both bbox.contains(point) and bbox.contains_inflated(point, params) — a hit against either drops the point into the dynamic bucket and breaks out of the box loop. insert_bounding_boxes() applies a flat inflate_margin to every incoming box before storing it.

docs.title: Velocity-inflated footprint
docs.text:
When a box carries a velocity, contains_inflated() doesn't grow a static margin — it shifts a 2D ellipse footprint along the XY velocity direction so the ellipse extends further ahead of the object than behind it, covering the volume it's expected to sweep before the next detection arrives. VelocityInflationParams is shared verbatim between Module 1 and Module 2 to avoid duplicating the same physics twice.

Struct field Config key Shipped value v_fwd_k velocity_inflation_k 0.85 v_rear_k rear_inflation_k, then overridden by reverse_velocity_inflation_k 0.35 (effective) v_lat_k lateral_inflation_k 0.30 v_vert_k vertical_inflation_k 0.20 — legacy, unused by the 2D footprint test v_min velocity_inflation_min 0.1 m/s activation floor v_max_speed velocity_inflation_max_speed 3.0 m/s saturation ellipse_box_cover_scale ellipse_box_cover_scale √2 — sized so the ellipse still covers the inflated box's corners

Config field ordering matters here

VelocityInflationParams::from_config() reads rear_inflation_k into v_rear_k first, then immediately re-reads reverse_velocity_inflation_k into the same field — the second read wins. config_bbox_rejection.json ships both keys (0.15 and 0.35 respectively); the effective rear multiplier is 0.35, not 0.15.

Config keys present but not read

config_bbox_rejection.json also ships bbox_potentially_dynamic_min_track_age, bbox_static_min_track_age, bbox_min_static_velocity and bbox_rejection_obstacle_min_removed_points. Only inflate_margin, max_bbox_frames, and the VelocityInflationParams fields above are actually consumed by dynamic_bounding_box_rejection.cpp / bounding_box.cpp — the other four are reserved for track-age gating logic that isn't wired up in this module yet.

docs.text: See config_bbox_rejection.json in the configuration reference for the full parameter table, including the shipped defaults above.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
All FIDO parameters share the same load pattern: Config config(GlobalConfig::get_config_path("config_<name>")), then config.param<T>("section", "key", default). A key missing from the JSON silently falls back to the C++ default, which often differs from the shipped value — the tables below list the shipped value. Comments (//, /* */) are stripped by glim::Config.

Status: active — used with effect at the shipped value · option — off by default, working · legacy — read but without effect (kept for old configs).

For how to tune them, see Tuning guide.

docs.title: Prerequisite
docs.text:
1. Install FIDO-GLIM and FIDO-GLIM-ROS2 following the installation section, or use the Docker images.
  2. Confirm your sensor and topic configuration in config/:
glim/config/config_ros.json
  "imu_topic": "/imu/data",
  "points_topic": "/velodyne_points",
  "bbox_topic": "/onboard_detector/tracked_dynamic_obstacles",
  "dynamic_rejection_type": "NONE",   // "NONE", "CLUSTER", "BBOX" or "COMBINED"
  "env_type": "INDOOR"                // "INDOOR" or "OUTDOOR"

Tip

dynamic_rejection_type is off ("NONE") by default — set it to "CLUSTER" (Module 1), "BBOX" (Module 2), or "COMBINED" (both) to actually enable FIDO. See FAQ for guidance on which to pick.

The rejection needs the raw scan

With dynamic_rejection_type other than "NONE" the preprocessor keeps the raw scan for the rejection (uniform 10k-point sample, far extra points, raw range images). Also check apply_lidar_imu_extrinsic and, without IMU, the CT odometry — see Configuration reference.

Warning

On ROS 2 you need to re-run colcon build to apply config changes in the installed package — use --symlink-install to avoid this.

docs.title: Executables
docs.text: glim_rosnode and glim_rosbag are provided by FIDO-GLIM-ROS2, the companion workspace package built on top of this repository's glim library:

docs.title: glim_rosnode
docs.text:
glim_rosnode launches GLIM (with FIDO's rejection stage running ahead of odometry, if enabled) as a standard ROS node subscribing to points, IMU, image and — when Module 2 is active — bounding-box topics.

ros2 run glim_ros glim_rosnode

docs.title: glim_rosbag
docs.text:
glim_rosbag reads directly from a rosbag, automatically adjusting playback speed to avoid data drop while mapping in minimum time.

ros2 run glim_ros glim_rosbag <bag_name>

Where the ROS node lives

This repository builds libglim.so and its plugin modules — the algorithms and the JSON config schema they read. glim_rosnode/glim_rosbag themselves, and the publishers for FIDO's diagnostic clouds, live in FIDO-GLIM-ROS2, a separate workspace package that links against this library — clone it alongside this repo, see Installation. See Architecture for exactly where FIDO's thread sits in that pipeline.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text:
GLIM reads parameters from JSON files in a config root directory (glim/config by default). It first reads config.json, which maps out relative paths to every submodule's parameter file, including five FIDO-specific ones:

{
  "global": {
    "config_wall_filter":               "config_wall_filter.json",
    "config_bbox_rejection":            "config_bbox_rejection.json",
    "config_dynamic_object_rejection":  "config_dynamic_object_rejection.json",
    "config_wall_registry":             "config_wall_registry.json",
    "config_dynamic_cluster_extractor": "config_dynamic_cluster_extractor.json"
  }
}

Comments (//, /* */) are allowed — glim::Config strips them before parsing, which is why every shipped file documents its own fields inline.

Info

See Configuration reference for every FIDO parameter, its default, and what reads it.

docs.title: What happens to a scan
docs.text:
Once dynamic_rejection_type is set, every incoming scan is split into a static frame (forwarded into GLIM's normal odometry path) and a dynamic frame (published separately for diagnostics/visualization) before it ever reaches scan matching. The full mechanics are in:

  • Architecture — the producer–consumer thread and its queues
  • Module 1 — Voxel pipeline — the autonomous filter, step by step
  • Tuning guide — adapting it to a new sensor or scene
  • Module 2 — Bounding box — the detector-driven filter

docs.title: Setup your own sensor
docs.text: FIDO adds no sensor-specific requirements beyond upstream GLIM. See the upstream Sensor setup guide.

docs.title: Tuning guide
docs.text: How to adapt Module 1 to a new sensor or scene. Effects: P = precision (fewer false positives), R = recall (fewer missed objects), ms = time. Every parameter is listed in the Configuration reference.

docs.title: 1 · Measure first
docs.text:
• With ground truth (HeLiMOS, SemanticKITTI, DOALS): P, R and IoU = TP / (TP + FP + FN) per range band (0–10, 10–20, 20–50 m), computed on the original scan points, not on GLIM's reordered output. The offline harness does exactly this.
  • Without ground truth, use proxies: share of points removed on stable structure (walls, poles) for false positives; flicker (points changing label between frames); share of points with free-space evidence that are removed, per range band, for recall.
  • Run-to-run noise. Parallel loops and a random RANSAC seed make identical runs differ by about ±0.7–1 IoU point. Compare on 2–3 runs, or set num_threads: 1 and wall_filter/rng_seed ≥ 0. A gain below one point from a single run is not reliable.
  • Two sequences: tune on one, check on the other.

docs.title: 2 · Recommended order
docs.text:
1. Pose and extrinsic. If they are wrong nothing else helps. Symptom: walls and façades removed, frequent "anomalous frame" guard. Check apply_lidar_imu_extrinsic and that the pose of the current scan is predicted (Module 1, step 0).
  2. Ground — ground_band_m, point_ground_cut, wall_filter/floor_polar_*.
  3. Sensor noise — noise_sigma* (see §4): it sets the dead zone of the centroid shift.
  4. Free space — visibility_*, fs_*: ages and resolution for your sensor and object speeds.
  5. Decision thresholds — cluster_propagation_threshold, track_evidence_bias, min_obj_height, min_obj_vis.
  6. Clustering — eps_voxel_factor, eps_range_k, frag_*, bbox_max_extent, only if objects look split or fused.
  7. Labelling — inflation in config_bbox_rejection.json, point_ground_cut, to move the P↔R balance.

docs.title: 3 · From symptom to parameter
docs.text: Symptom Look at Walls/façades removed, "everything moves" pose prediction, apply_lidar_imu_extrinsic; then pose_err_* False positives on the ground ground_band_m, point_ground_cut, wall_filter/floor_* False positives on vegetation and edges visibility_abs_thr ↑, fs_min_free ↑, min_obj_height ↑, track_evidence_bias ↑ Furniture or parked objects removed long after they stopped locked_struct_frac, permanent_release_no_motion_frames, locked_max_height Slow or far pedestrians never caught visibility_*_age ↑, noise_deadzone_k ↓, hybrid_*, vac_* Objects caught late min_dynamic_frames 1, fast_confirm_* ↓, track_evidence_on ↓ Objects flickering track_evidence_decay ↑, fut_delay (offline) Objects split into pieces frag_merge_gap ↑; on sparse sensors eps_range_k People fused with walls or poles eps_voxel_factor ↓ Cars not caught bbox_max_extent (4 m is the limit; 6.5 m cost 4 IoU points on HeLiMOS) Trails behind objects velocity_inflation_k ↓, track_bbox_history_size ↓ Too slow hybrid_max_points ↓, fs_ray_stride ↑, fs_max_range ↓, cluster_max_range ↓, visibility_res_deg ↑

docs.title: 4 · A new sensor
docs.text:
1. Centroid noise (noise_sigma0, noise_sigma_slope): with the robot still in a static scene, measure the voxel-centroid shift between frames at several ranges. σ0 ≈ the value close to the sensor, slope ≈ growth per metre.
  2. Range-image resolution (visibility_res_deg): about the angular spacing of the points actually used (after sampling), or slightly coarser. Too fine leaves holes; too coarse lets an object cover its own past.
  3. Vertical filter on sparse rings (visibility_min_filter_rows): with 16–32 rings the image has empty rows between rings; set the vertical half-size to about ring spacing / resolution (VLP-16 at 0.5°: 4).
  4. Free-space ages: a pedestrian (~1.3 m/s) must move at least 2–3 pixels at the range you care about. At 15 m and 0.5° a pixel is ~0.13 m, so ≥ 0.3–0.4 m, i.e. ≥ 0.3 s.
  5. Clustering on sparse rings (eps_range_k): ≈ 1.15 × vertical ring spacing in radians, so the rings of one person still connect far away.
  6. Density: rej_input_points, hybrid_*, min_pts.
  7. Mounting: sensor height (ground), cluster_max_height, ground_band_m, max_obj_bottom_hag / max_obj_top_hag.
  8. Only then the decision thresholds (§2, step 5).

docs.title: 5 · Method
docs.text:
• One parameter at a time, 3–4 values (×0.5, ×1, ×1.5, ×2), compared per range band.
  • Watch the video of the extreme variants: understanding why something changes is worth more than +0.3 IoU.
  • Diagnose by category before touching parameters. Missed points: no cluster · static cluster · dynamic but not confirmed · confirmed but not removed. False positives: ground in the box · inflated zone · non-existent object. The harness option --diag 1 writes the per-box decision inputs needed for this.
  • Automatic search once single parameters are sensible: random or Bayesian search (e.g. Optuna) over 8–12 parameters, IoU < 20 m on the tuning sequence as objective with a time constraint, checked on the other sequence.
  • Upper bounds: replace one stage at a time with ground truth (clusters, tracking, decision) to know where work pays off. On HeLiMOS: perfect per-cluster decision → 84.6 IoU, perfect tracking → 81.2.

docs.title: 6 · Reference configurations
docs.text: Scenario Changes from the defaults Vehicle outdoor, Ouster 128 (HeLiMOS) defaults Offline mapping, best IoU fut_delay: 10, fut_output_delayed: true Indoor robot, low speeds track_evidence_on: -1 if stable structure gets removed; ground_band_m 0.15–0.2 Sparse sensor (16–32 rings) visibility_res_deg 0.7–1°, visibility_min_filter_rows ≈ ring spacing / resolution, eps_range_k (VLP-16 0.04), min_pts 1–2, re-tune noise_sigma* Limited time budget fs_enabled: false, hybrid_max_points 4000, cluster_max_range 40
